newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK FINMIN'S TREASURY EXPERT QUITS IN FRUSTRATION.
newsitem.headline: GREEK FINMIN'S TREASURY EXPERT QUITS IN FRUSTRATION.

text.p: Christofer Sardelis, the finance ministry's treasury expert who was brought in from Sweden to set up and run the state treasury's debt management office, resigned today, ministry sources told Reuters.
In his resignation letter, Sardelis cited "the lack of work objective" as the main reason for his decision to resign, the sources said.

Sardelis took over the post at the finance ministry last August after accepting an invitation from former Finance Minister and current Interior Minister Alexandros Papadopoulos to take the job and help manage Greece's public debt.

Sardelis had served as director of the economic research department at the central bank of Sweden for eight years and was chief treasury economist at the largest private Swedish bank, Svenska Handelsbanken, from March 1995.
Greece has the third highest debt to GDP ratio in the European Union but its interest payments on public debt are the EU's highest as a percentage of GDP.

The finance ministry has said it will set up an economic analysis unit to process data and prepare proposals that will be presented to the Greek public debt management committee. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
